topic: methotrexate early rheumatoid arthritis combination therapy TEAR
synopsis: TEAR enrolled adults with rheumatoid arthritis of less than 3 years who met 1987 ACR criteria and had active disease. Everyone received oral methotrexate, escalated to 20 mg per week by week 12 unless disease was already quiet at a lower dose. The four arms were immediate etanercept plus methotrexate, immediate triple therapy with methotrexate, sulfasalazine, and hydroxychloroquine, or methotrexate alone with step-up at week 24 to etanercept or to sulfasalazine plus hydroxychloroquine if DAS28-ESR was still at least 3.2. The trial is described as the only randomized double-blind comparison of oral triple therapy with etanercept plus methotrexate. The primary outcome showed no difference between those two approaches. Twenty-eight percent of participants had an excellent response to methotrexate monotherapy and reached low disease activity by 6 months. At week 102, the only significant treatment difference reported was ACR70, 18.2% with etanercept versus 11.3% with triple therapy (p=0.02). Modified HAQ improved similarly across groups.
